Article Title: ‘Global order under stress’: Jaishankar calls for stronger multilateralism at UNGA
Article Text:
EAM S Jaishankar during P4M Summit

External affairs minister S Jaishankar called for stronger multilateralism to navigate rising geopolitical tensions, conflicts and global competition, as he co-chaired the first Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace & Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa on Monday (local time). The summit was held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.Minister Jaishankar stressed the need for greater international cooperation and called for steps to address ongoing conflicts, create safeguards for emerging technologies and reduce risks linked to dominance and disruption. He also stressed the importance of international law, rules and norms.In a post on X, Jaishankar said the summit provided an opportunity to underline the importance of multilateralism at a time when international cooperation is facing pressure from intense competition, geopolitical tensions and conflicts.He highlighted the need to address the specific dimensions of ongoing conflicts, establish frameworks and safeguards for emerging capabilities, and reduce risks by diversifying against dominance and disruption. He also underlined the importance of international law, rules and norms.The EAM further called for “reformed multilateralism”, saying more participative discussions and transparent decision-making could help restore hope in the UN system and strengthen countries’ resolve to work together.Addressing the summit, Jaishankar thanked European Council President Antonio Costa for initiating the forum and said India was pleased to join as a co-sponsor. He said the global order was under stress, with a long-running rebalancing of the world taking a different shape amid intensifying competition, geopolitical tensions and conflicts.He said that if these pressures were left unchecked, they could undermine the spirit of international cooperation, making it crucial for multilateralism to assert itself more strongly."We meet at a time when the global order is under stress. For some decades, the world has witnessed a steady rebalancing, which was a long-expected structural evolution. However, extreme competition, geopolitical tensions, and actual conflicts have given this an entirely different character. If left unchecked, it would call into question the very spirit of international cooperation. That is why it is so essential that multilateralism asserts itself strongly at this juncture. "Jaishankar also highlighted the range of issues that he said depended on countries' willingness to cooperate, including peace and international security, climate action and climate justice, emerging technologies, development finance, countering terrorism, strengthening supply chains, disaster resilience and pandemic preparedness."At stake here are very real issues, not just words and expressions. The future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance, of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chains, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics. All depend on a will to cooperate."The summit also saw Jaishankar make a case for Reformed Multilateralism, with participative deliberations and transparent decision-making being highlighted as ways to provide hope and optimism to the UN system and reinforce countries' resolve to work together.Meanwhile, Slovakia backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council on Monday, with foreign minister Juraj Blanár saying India, as a leading country of the Global South and an emerging power in the Indo-Pacific, should have a place at the UN's top decision-making body.Blanar's remarks came after Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York."We all agree, as V4 countries, that India, as part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," Blanár said.The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week.Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion". Discussions covered political, economic, defence, technology, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties.Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the 81st UN General Assembly high-level week in New York and is scheduled to address the General Debate on September 26.
Article Summary: Eam s jaishankar called for stronger multilateralism to navigate rising geopolitical tensions, conflicts and global competition. He co-chaired the first partners for multilateralism, international law, peace & prosperity summit with european council president antonio costa.

Article Title: Xi suffered stroke & fainted at Brics Summit, claims China Democracy Party chief; post gets community note

Wanjun Xie, chairman of the China Democratic Party, has claimed in a post on X that Chinese president Xi Jinping fainted during the Brics summit hosted by New Delhi and was taken back to China on a special flight for medical treatment.Xie claimed that after receiving emergency treatment from his accompanying medical team, Xi ended his visit to India early and returned to China on a special plane.According to the post, upon the plane's arrival at Beijing airport, authorities did not arrange for a large group of officials to greet Xi or organise a welcome ceremony. Article Title: WHO puts stroke, cancer, mental health on 10-year traditional medicine research agenda
Article Text:
The World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade. (Photo: @WHO)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From stroke and cancer to mental health and pain management, the World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade.Its 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth as priority areas. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included.The report highlights a striking mismatch between disease burden and research. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition. Mental health ranks eighth among contributors to disability-adjusted life years, but the review found very few or no grants specifically focused on mental health conditions. Musculoskeletal conditions are also a prominent cause of disability globally but remain under-researched relative to their burden.Cancer, too, features among the priority areas, with the report noting rising global incidence and calling for research into integrative oncology and palliative care.For metabolic health and endocrine disorders, WHO identifies the need for stronger evidence, including longer-term studies on conditions such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome.WHO says the aim is to generate stronger evidence on effectiveness, safety, regulation and health-system integration so countries can make informed decisions about the role of these approaches in healthcareThe research agenda also puts patient safety under the spotlight. It calls for studies on herb-drug interactions, monitoring and reporting of adverse events, regulatory and quality-assurance systems, and the safe integration of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine into primary healthcare.The push comes against a broader funding gap. WHO says traditional, complementary and integrative medicine is widely used globally, with use reaching up to 80% of populations in some settings, while less than 1% of global health research funding is directed towards research in the field.India has a direct connection to the agenda. The WHO report acknowledges financial support from the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, for its development and publication. India was also among the health ministries that participated in the Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine, held in New Delhi in December 2025.The report, however, is a research-prioritisation framework rather than a clinical guideline or recommendation to use any particular traditional medicine.
Article Summary: The world health organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine. Stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth are priority areas.

Article Title: 4 European nations back India's bid for permanent UN seat, Jaishankar calls it 'historic'
Article Text:
Image credit: X/ Jaishankar

Jaishankar on V4's role in global affairs

India, V4 agree on closer cooperation

Poland, Hungry, Slovakia and Czech Republic on Monday backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, with Slovakia foreign minister Juraj Blanár saying India, as a leading country of the Global South and an emerging power in the Indo-Pacific, should have a place at the UN's top decision-making body.The remarks came after external affairs minister S Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York."We all agree, as V4 countries, that India, as part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," Blanár said.The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week.Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion" and said the discussions covered political, economic, defence, technology, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties."We had our first Visegrad Four and India meeting. It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion, and I would like to thank Minister Juraj (Foreign Minister of Slovakia) for convening us today. It was a very, very productive meeting.What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4, we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum. As foreign ministers, we would meet annually. That was the consensus. We would also explore in technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defense. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation. We discussed space issues, connectivity, and people-to-people mobility. We have students in each of the V4 countries. Overall, in terms of our cooperation, as well as a very good and useful exchange on the big global crisis, the Ukraine conflict, and what's happening in the Gulf. I think it was a very worthwhile and productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it."Asked about the political importance of the V4 for India on the global stage, Jaishankar said New Delhi viewed the four countries as partners with strong industrial, technological and innovation capabilities."We have very good relations with the V4 countries, and we know that these are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. They are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent. And I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work."India has been seeking reform of the UN Security Council and a permanent seat on the body. The Council currently has five permanent members, China, France, Russia, the UK and the US, alongside 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.Jaishankar had formally launched India's campaign for a non-permanent UNSC term for 2028-29 in July, while New Delhi has continued to press for broader reform of the Council and permanent membership for India.Jaishankar said the meeting also resulted in an agreement to strengthen cooperation through annual foreign ministerial meetings and an annual business forum.In a post on X, Jaishankar said: "Our first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to: Closer political cooperation including annual meetings of Foreign Ministers. Deeper economic cooperation, including the Annual Business Forum. Reinvigorating our defence cooperation. Further development of our cultural cooperation and people-to-people relations."The meeting included Poland's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, Hungary's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Dr Anita Orbán, Slovakia's foreign minister Juraj Blanár and Czechia's foreign minister Petr Macinka.Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the 81st UN General Assembly high-level week in New York and is scheduled to address the General Debate on September 26.
Article Summary: Poland, hungry, slovakia and czech republic back india's bid for a permanent seat on the united nations security council. External affairs minister s jaishankar participated in the first high-level visegrád group (v4) plus india meeting on the sidelines of un general assembly.

Article Title: Lt Gen Mohit Seth to be new GOC of White Knight Corps
Article Text:
Maj Gen Mohit Seth took over as the General Officer Commanding (GOC) relieving Maj Gen SS Slaria who has moved to Headquarter Northern Command.

JAMMU: Lieutenant General Mohit Seth will take over as the new General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Army’s Nagrota-based White Knight Corps (16 Corps) on Oct 1. He will replace Lt Gen P K Mishra, who will move to a new posting, officials said.In his distinguished military career spanning over three decades, Lt Gen Seth has served in key command and staff positions in J&K, the northeast, and at the Army HQ. He is currently the Commandant of the Indian Military Training Team in Bhutan.Lt Gen Seth previously was GOC of the Counter-Insurgency Force Kilo (Kilo Force), an elite formation of the Army’s Rashtriya Rifles tasked with anti-terror operations in north Kashmir. He has also served as the Indian Army Liaison Officer at the High Commission of India, United Kingdom.
Article Summary: Lt gen mohit seth will take over as the new general officer commanding (goc) of the army’s nagrota-based white knight corps (16 corps) he will replace lt gen p k mishra, who will move to a new posting.

Article Title: 'No burden for consumers': Sitharaman clarifies who will pay MDR on UPI transactions
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has backed the recently announced Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), saying that the mechanism will be imposed on operators and will not be passed on to customers. Addressing ongoing speculations around the charges, FM blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.Speaking to ANI, the finance minister said that she had already addressed the issue in Parliament, stressing that MDR is a charge between payment operators and will not be 'burdened' on UPI users.Sitharaman stressed that MDR is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the Consolidated Fund of India.”It does not apply to transactions below Rs 2,000. It is neither a tax nor a cess; the funds will not be deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India. It is a charge levied by service providers to improve the system and provide better service, not for small transactions. Moreover, it is a charge between operators; it will not be passed on to the consumer. The burden does not fall on the customer,” she said.Sitharaman said she had given the same clarification earlier too, when the issue came up during the parliamentary session.“I provided a clarification on this very point when the issue was raised during the parliamentary session. Spreading misinformation, fueling debates based on it, and using that narrative to attack the government has become a habit for the opposition. This is wrong; there is an effort to spread misconceptions and mislead the public. The public needs to remain vigilant," Sitharaman added.Meanwhile, Niti Aayog NITI Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri had also backed the Centre’s decision to introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions, saying that businesses should find ways to sustain themselves instead of relying on government subsidies.Lahiri drew on the words of ancient philosopher Chanakya to make his point, saying a ruler should collect taxes from citizens as a bee collects honey from a flower — “gently, gradually, and without inflicting pain or bruising the petals”.“So you have to find ways of sustaining businesses without having to give subsidy,” Lahiri told reporters on the sidelines of an event.He clarified that the view was his personal opinion and did not represent NITI Aayog’s official position.The government has ruled out any rethink on the decision, with a senior official telling PTI, “There is no question of a re-think.”FM Sitharaman’s clarification comes after the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) introduced a new MDR framework on September 15. Under the framework, an MDR of 0.4 per cent will apply to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, subject to a cap of Rs 300 per transaction.Consumers will continue to transact free of cost using UPI. The government has said that around 96 per cent of P2M transactions will remain unaffected, while the MDR will be distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers.
Article Summary: Finance minister nirmala sitharaman has backed the recently announced merchant discount rate (mdr) she stressed that mdr is neither a tax nor a cess and that the money collected through it will not go into the consolidated fund of india. Fm blamed the opposition for creating confusion and urged people to remain alert.

Article Title: Watch: Press pool boycott leaves Trump barely audible at White House event
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view How do you prefer to get updates about government activities? Television news Online news websites Social media Official government channels 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

US President Donald Trump was barely audible during live coverage of a White House event on Monday after major television networks suspended pooled coverage following his decision to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.During the event, Trump unveiled a new helipad on the White House South Lawn and spoke with construction workers. However, the sound of Marine One drowned out much of his speech with TV pool cameras and microphones absent.In a video shared bu Clash Report, Trump was seen cutting a ribbon on the walkway leading to the new helipad and interacting with workers. His comments, however, were inaudible on the White House livestream.Meanwhile, the White House subsequently launched 'Trump TV', a 24/7 streaming platform featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and coverage related to the US President.The five networks that make up the White House TV pool - ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC - suspended pooled coverage after Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds, citing “fake news”.“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government.No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting,” the five networks said in a joint statement.The White House press pool is a rotating group of journalists who travel with the president and share reporting, audio and video with other news organisations. With the TV pool absent, there was no standard pool microphone or live feed to clearly capture Trump’s remarks during the helipad event.C-SPAN also said it would not air the ceremony because it relies on the TV pool and did not have a feed.The White House later launched “Trump TV”, a 24/7 streaming platform featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other coverage related to Trump.The episode highlighted the immediate impact of the White House’s press restrictions, with little independent broadcast footage available from the helipad event in the absence of the TV pool.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump was barely audible during live coverage of a white house event on monday after major television networks suspended pooled coverage. During the event, trump unveiled a new helipad on the white house south lawn and spoke with construction workers.

Article Title: UK backs Saudi Arabia with RAF Voyager refuelling support amid Houthi campaign
Article Text:
File photo: Andy Burnham

UK links support to energy security

Britain stops short of direct strikes

The UK has stated that it will provide Saudi Arabia with defensive military support, including air-to-air refuelling for Saudi fighter jets, as Riyadh faces a renewed campaign of attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen.Prime minister Andy Burnham said Saudi Arabia had requested military support and that Britain had agreed to provide an RAF Voyager aircraft to refuel Saudi jets for several weeks.The aircraft is expected to operate from RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. British officials described the deployment as “time limited” and said it was intended to help Saudi Arabia defend its energy infrastructure and keep key oil routes open.The move comes as the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and taken control of the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, a major maritime route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.Burnham said the decision was partly driven by concerns over the impact of the conflict on energy supplies and the cost of living in Britain.“I go back to the point I made about cost-of-living pressures and acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region,” Burnham told reporters from BBC.Saudi Arabia has faced a series of Houthi attacks in recent days, including missile and drone strikes targeting Riyadh and energy infrastructure along the Red Sea coast.The attacks have raised concerns over further disruption to Saudi oil exports.The UK already provides air-defence support to Saudi Arabia, including the deployment of the Sky Sabre system. The new refuelling mission will allow Saudi aircraft to remain airborne for longer while responding to incoming threats.The deployment is significantly more limited than Britain's previous military action against the Houthis.In January 2024, the UK joined the US in carrying out airstrikes against Houthi military targets in Yemen after the group attacked commercial shipping in the Red Sea. Further British-American strikes followed later that year.This time, the UK has framed its involvement as defensive support rather than direct attacks on Houthi positions.The announcement also comes as Burnham prepares for his first face-to-face meeting with US President Donald Trump at the UN. Burnham said he would urge Trump to work towards ending the war in Iran, arguing that the conflict and the wider instability in the Middle East were contributing to economic pressure in Britain.The UK government is also concerned about the wider consequences of the fighting for global energy and shipping routes. The Bab al-Mandab Strait has become a new flashpoint after the Houthis' recent advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast, while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted.Burnham said Britain wanted to see the conflict end as quickly as possible and was ready to work with its allies to reduce the wider instability.
Article Summary: Uk to provide air-to-air refuelling for saudi fighter jets. Move comes as riyadh faces renewed campaign of attacks by iran-backed houthi forces in yemen. Decision driven by concerns over impact of conflict on energy supplies and cost of living in britain.

Article Title: Will shut Iranian flights from Wednesday: US new arm-twist move against Tehran
Article Text:
The warning came as the Trump administration expands its sanctions campaign aimed at restricting Iran’s access to international financial and commercial networks

US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said Iranian airlines could "effectively be shut out of global operations" from Wednesday and threatened foreign companies providing services to Tehran’s aviation sector with secondary sanctions.Bessent on Monday said, “on September 23, all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world”.“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets, or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” Bessent said, according to Al Jazeera.The warning comes as the Trump administration expands its sanctions campaign aimed at restricting Iran’s access to international financial and commercial networks.Earlier this month, the US treasury department imposed sanctions on additional Iranian airlines as well as companies outside Iran accused of supporting Tehran’s aviation sector.Iran’s aviation industry has already faced years of US sanctions, limiting Iranian carriers’ ability to acquire new aircraft and access spare parts and maintenance services.The latest measures are part of a broader US sanctions regime targeting Iran’s economy, including its energy, shipping, technology, gold and digital-asset sectors.Secondary sanctions can subject foreign companies doing business with sanctioned Iranian entities to restrictions on access to the US financial system.Bessent’s comments came a day after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.China is a key economic partner and diplomatic supporter of Iran, making Beijing’s cooperation significant to Washington’s efforts to restrict Tehran’s access to international finance.According to Al Jazeera, Bessent said Chinese officials had been “very engaged” in discussions over the US pressure campaign. He also said Washington was holding positive talks with Chinese financial authorities, including People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, on compliance with US sanctions targeting Iran.
Article Summary: Us treasury secretary scott bessent said iranian airlines could "effectively be shut out of global operations" from wednesday. The warning comes as the trump administration expands its sanctions campaign aimed at restricting iran’s access to international financial and commercial networks.

Article Title: South Korea proposes nuclear freeze with Kim Jong Un in exchange for sanctions relief: Report
Article Text:
South Korea's Lee urges Trump to seek nuclear freeze deal with North Korea (file photo)

Why Lee wants a nuclear freeze first

North Korea has more leverage now

South Korean president Lee Jae Myung has urged US president Donald Trump to seek a nuclear freeze deal with North Korea instead of insisting on immediate denuclearisation, arguing that sanctions have failed to stop North Korea from expanding its weapons programmes.In an interview with the New York Times, Lee said Washington could offer sanctions relief in exchange for Pyongyang halting further development of nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology.“I believe there is significant value in a trade-off between sanctions –– which are not particularly effective anyway –– and a stop to the development of additional nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology,” Lee told NYT.Lee argued that demanding complete denuclearisation under current circumstances would achieve little, as North Korea has continued to expand its nuclear capabilities while strengthening ties with Russia and China.“Aiming for denuclearisation under the current circumstances guarantees that nothing will be accomplished,” he said.Lee’s proposal would make a nuclear freeze the first step, followed by reciprocal incentives and concessions aimed at building trust with Pyongyang.He said the longer-term goal would be to create conditions in which North Korea feels secure enough to eventually reduce and give up its nuclear arsenal.The South Korean president believes Trump is uniquely positioned to restart talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, given the two leaders’ previous personal diplomacy. Trump met Kim three times during his first term, including a 2019 meeting at the inter-Korean border, but those talks failed to produce an agreement.Lee said the alternative to diplomacy was increasingly risky as North Korea continued to expand its nuclear arsenal.“Our estimates suggest that North Korea is now capable of producing, or may already be producing, an additional 10 to 20 nuclear weapons each year,” he said, warning that Pyongyang could eventually be tempted to export nuclear weapons and missiles for money.Lee’s push comes as North Korea has moved closer to Russia and China and become less dependent on negotiations with Seoul or Washington.Pyongyang has deployed troops and weapons to support Russia’s war in Ukraine, strengthening its relationship with Moscow. North Korea has also deepened ties with Beijing, while its economy has shown signs of growth.That has given Kim more room to resist pressure from Washington. North Korea has also continued developing its nuclear and missile capabilities despite Trump’s efforts to revive diplomacy.North Korea has also been regularly carrying out military exercises and testing its arsenal of ballistic missiles near South Korean waters, worsening tensions in a region already plagued by military tensions and a long-running standoff between the two Koreas.Trump had also recently scaled back a major US-South Korean military exercise, describing such drills as hostile toward Kim. North Korea has nevertheless continued weapons activity, including recent ballistic missile launches.Lee is not alone in arguing for a shift towards a phased approach. Stephen E Biegun, who served as the US special representative for North Korea during Trump’s first term, recently said Washington could negotiate a “slowing or freezing” of North Korea’s nuclear arsenal.But North Korea has repeatedly signalled that it does not intend to give up its nuclear arsenal, making any freeze deal potentially difficult to negotiate.Lee nevertheless believes a freeze would be a more realistic starting point than demanding complete denuclearisation at the outset.
Article Summary: South korea's lee urges trump to seek nuclear freeze deal with north korea. Lee argues that sanctions have failed to stop north korea from expanding its weapons programmes. Lee’s proposal would make a nuclear freeze the first step, followed by reciprocal incentives and concessions aimed at building trust.

Article Title: Muhammad Ali’s 1915 Los Angeles mansion was bought for $2.5 million in 2001, restored while retaining its Tiffany stained glass, listed for nearly $17 million and finally sold for $8.5 million in 2024
Article Text:
Historic estate in gated Fremont Place

Historic architecture and interior features

Market history and final auction sale

The Real Deal

Legacy of the Fremont Place community

The former Los Angeles home of three-time world heavyweight boxing champion Muhammad Ali, a 1915 Italian Renaissance mansion in the gated Fremont Place community, sold for $8.5 million (£6.7 million) in July 2024. The sale ended a long period on the market for the historic property. The house was first listed for almost $17 million ($16.995 million) in late 2022 before going through several price cuts and eventually being offered at auction.Located at 55 Fremont Place near Hancock Park, the 11,545-square-foot estate sits on about 1.6 acres. Architect John C. Austin, who also designed Los Angeles City Hall and the Griffith Observatory, designed the home, which was built in 1915. Ali lived in the mansion during the late 1970s and 1980s with his third wife, Veronica, and their daughters, Laila and Hana. During his time there, the house welcomed many well-known guests, including world leaders, entertainers and sports stars. The estate has nine bedrooms and seven bathrooms in the main house. A separate guest house adds another bedroom and full bathroom. The grounds also include a heated swimming pool, spa, landscaped lawns, stone paths and a large outdoor patio for entertaining.Developer Michael R. Kaplan and his wife, Tari, bought the property in 2001 for about $2.5 million. They spent several years restoring the home, updating its modern systems while keeping many of its original architectural details. The preserved features include original Tiffany stained-glass windows, French Empire crystal chandeliers and carved wooden wall panels. The house also has marble and hardwood floors, several fireplaces, hand-carved mouldings and large bay windows. According to real estate listing records published by Zillow and Redfin, the mansion includes a glass-domed sunroom, a formal dining room with historic light fixtures, a main bedroom with two dressing rooms, a media room and a full cellar.After the renovations were completed, the owners first listed the property for $16 million in August 2021. The listing was later withdrawn and returned to the market in November 2022 with a higher asking price of $16.995 million. According to, a Los Angeles real estate news publication, the price was lowered to $15 million in early 2023. When no buyer agreed to that price, the owners decided to put the property up for auction with no minimum price in May 2024 through Concierge Auctions. Property records maintained by Zillow show that the sale officially closed on July 18, 2024, for $8.5 million. That was about 50 per cent below the property's 2022 asking price.Fremont Place is one of Los Angeles' oldest private gated communities. It was established in 1911 in the Mid-Wilshire area near Hancock Park. The neighborhood has 73 single-family homes, many designed by well-known 20th-century architects. Over the years, the community has been home to Hollywood stars, business leaders and civic officials. Redfin property records show that homes in the area continue to command high prices, with 55 Fremont Place among the community's largest properties. The July 2024 sale transferred ownership of the historic mansion for the first time in 23 years, bringing a new chapter to one of Hancock Park's best-known historic homes.
Article Summary: Historic estate in gated fremont place sold for $8.5 million (£6.7 million) the sale ended a long period on the market for the historic property. The house was first listed for almost $17 million ($16.995 million) in late 2022 before going through several price cuts and eventually being offered at auction.

Article Title: Amid Trump’s clash with CNN, Politico, MS NOW, White House launches ‘Trump TV’
Article Text:
White House launches 24/7 ‘TRUMP TV’ amid press access battle

The White House on Monday launched ‘TRUMP TV: The Essentials Station’, a 24/7 digital video stream featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other content, as the Trump administration faces a legal challenge from CNN, MS NOW and Politico over their exclusion from the White House.The White House said the new service would bring the administration's "biggest moments" together in one place, with content updated in real time. The stream was launched on the White House's YouTube channel at 7 pm ET on Monday.The launch came hours after CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration, seeking to restore their access to the White House. The organisations argue that the administration's decision to revoke their journalists' credentials violates their First Amendment rights.Trump had barred the three outlets from the White House after criticising their coverage. Their reporters were denied entry to the White House grounds on Saturday and had their press credentials confiscated, according to the organisations.CNN was also removed from its scheduled television pool duties. ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC subsequently joined CNN in suspending their participation in the White House television pool after CNN was removed from a scheduled assignment.The television pool normally provides shared video coverage of presidential events to broadcasters and other news organisations. Article Title: Pakistan airstrikes on Afghanistan: 3 killed, several injured as conflict fears grow
Article Text:
Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along border. (AP photo/ File)

Taliban warns of 'crushing response'

Kabul denies sheltering TTP

Afghanistan keeps door open for talks

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the main focus for Pakistan and Afghanistan in resolving their issues? Diplomatic negotiations Border security Intelligence sharing Ceasing cross-border operations 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

At least three people were killed and several others injured in a Pakistani airstrike targeting Afghanistan's northeastern Kunar province, Tolo News reported on Monday, citing a provincial official.The military strike is supposedly in retaliation for suicide bombing at a police station compound in northwestern Pakistan, raising fears that tensions between the neighbouring nations could once again turn into open fighting.Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action.Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, ahead of the imminent Pakistani strikes, had warned Islamabad against carrying out strikes inside Afghanistan, saying Kabul would respond militarily if its territory is attacked.In an interview with Al Arabiya English, Mujahid rejected Pakistan's allegations that militant groups based in Afghanistan recruit, train and launch attacks against Pakistan.“If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” Mujahid said.He said any Pakistani military operation inside Afghanistan would amount to a violation of Afghan sovereignty and could trigger a strong response from Kabul.Mujahid was responding to comments by a Pakistani military spokesperson, who had told Al Arabiya English that militant groups were using Afghan territory to recruit, train and arm fighters before sending them into Pakistan.Mujahid rejected those allegations and said the Taliban administration does not allow the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , or TTP, to operate from Afghan soil.He also denied that the Taliban government supports armed groups carrying out attacks against other countries. Instead, Mujahid said Pakistan should examine its own internal security problems, arguing that violence involving the TTP and Baloch armed groups existed before the Taliban returned to power in 2021.Pakistan has repeatedly accused militant groups of operating from Afghanistan and has pressed Kabul to take action against them. The Taliban has consistently denied allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.Despite his warning of military retaliation, Mujahid said Kabul was still willing to engage with Islamabad through dialogue.He called for stronger intelligence-sharing arrangements and greater bilateral cooperation to address security concerns along the two countries' border.Mujahid also backed a possible mediation role for Saudi Arabia, saying Riyadh has good relations with both Afghanistan and Pakistan and could help the two sides resolve their differences.Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border. The latest airstrike, coming amid fresh security concerns, risks further worsening those ties and could lead to another confrontation between the neighbours.
Article Summary: Relations between kabul and islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along border. The latest escalation comes days after the taliban warned that it would defend afghan territory against any pakistani military action. The taliban has consistently denied allowing afghan territory to be used for attacks against pakistan.

Article Title: Iran war risk: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns of oil shocks, sticky inflation and higher interest rates
Article Text: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned that the ongoing war in Iran could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated and pushing interest rates higher than current market expectations, Reuters reported.The warning came in his annual letter to shareholders, a day after US President Donald Trump escalated pressure on Iran by threatening to target key infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened."Now, because of the war in Iran, we additionally face the potential for significant ongoing oil and commodity price shocks, along with the reshaping of global supply chains, which may lead to stickier inflation and ultimately higher interest rates than markets currently expect," Dimon said, news agency Reuters quoted as saying.Dimon, who has led JPMorgan for two decades, also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China."The challenges we all face are significant," he added.He said it remains uncertain whether the Iran war will achieve US objectives, while warning that nuclear proliferation remains the biggest risk linked to Iran.Markets have already begun pricing in these risks, with expectations of interest rate cuts this year largely fading amid rising inflation concerns triggered by the conflict.Last week, the benchmark S&P 500 index recorded its worst quarterly performance since 2022, weighed down by rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty since late February.Dimon noted that the US economy remains resilient, with consumers continuing to earn and spend, and businesses staying broadly healthy, though signs of weakening have emerged.He cautioned that economic strength has been supported by significant government deficit spending and past stimulus, while infrastructure investment needs continue to grow.At the same time, he pointed to positives such as fiscal stimulus under President Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill", deregulation policies and rising capital expenditure driven by artificial intelligence.On financial stability, Dimon said the $1.8-trillion private credit market "probably" does not pose a systemic risk, despite investor concerns and recent withdrawals from such funds.However, he warned that in a downturn, losses across leveraged lending could exceed expectations as credit standards have weakened.Private credit markets also lack transparency and rigorous valuation benchmarks, increasing the risk of investor exits if conditions worsen, he said.Separately, Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical" and "very flawed".He said JPMorgan’s GSIB surcharge would fall only to 5.0%, a level he described as “absurd” and “un-American”, arguing it penalises the bank’s scale and performance.
Article Summary: Jpmorgan chase ceo jamie dimon warns iran war could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated. He also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in ukraine, tensions in the middle east and friction with china. Dimon criticised revised us capital rules, including basel iii and gsib surcharge norms.

Article Title: How selling Alaska in 1867 was a costly mistake for Russia
Article Text:
Image: Wikipedia

Why Russia agreed to the Alaska purchase

The hidden wealth Russia gave away

Strategic and geopolitical consequences

In 1867, Russia’s decision to sell Alaska to America turned out to be a historic mistake that was to go unnoticed for years to come. The sum paid by the US was only $7,200,000. Although, in the light of the circumstances at the time, it appeared logical, retrospectively, the act looks extremely shortsighted. Russia found itself economically constrained, geographically far away from the region and fearful of its falling into the hands of the British without any compensation. In reality, however, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the United States.The choice of selling Alaska was based on economic and political reasons. By the middle of the 19th century, the Russian Empire experienced financial difficulties as a result of the expensive Crimean War. It had become increasingly hard for the country to manage such remote and thinly populated areas as Alaska.According to EBSCO , “the Russian-American Company was in decline, and the colony failed to yield any profit”.In addition to this, the lucrative fur trade had declined, making the territory much less economically valuable for the empire.At the same time, Russia was afraid that Britain might capture Alaska in case another war broke out between the two countries. Selling the colony to the friendly United States appeared as a logical step. As the Office of the Historian states, William H. Seward, U.S. Secretary of State, “it was a chance to expand its influence in North America and hinder further growth of Britain”.For Russia, the transaction was a chance to minimise the losses. However, it greatly undervalued the potential of Alaska.Another thing that Russia did not expect was the amount of riches that Alaska possessed. Within several decades after the acquisition, the state saw discoveries of enormous deposits of gold, oil, and other minerals.“Alaska has produced more than 40 million ounces of gold,” according to the US Geological Survey. Furthermore, Alaska is home to some of the world's most significant undeveloped mineral deposits, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) . But even more importantly, the state's oil deposits turned out to be extremely valuable. The Prudhoe Bay oil field was discovered in 1968 and became one of North America's biggest.In retrospect, the amount paid by the Americans, $7.2 million, or two cents per acre, was rather laughable. According to Howard I. Kushner , the deal “robbed Russia of an enormously rich territory, the true value of which would only be recognised in the twentieth century.”In addition to resources, there is the question of strategy and how important Alaska is to the United States from a strategic standpoint. This is a very good place when it comes to defence strategy. It borders on the Arctic Ocean and also happens to be close to Russia.During the period of the Cold War, the Alaskan region became a frontier area for the United States, becoming home to military facilities and warning systems.According to Col. Michael J. Forsyth, U.S. Army, the closeness of Russia and Alaska, only about ninety kilometres apart across the Bering Strait, meant that this region became highly significant to the United States' defence plans.From today's point of view, the strategic location of Alaska makes the state very important to the policies of the U.S. related to the Arctic, energy security, and even environmental policies.Thinking back, what seems clear to us now is that the Russians sold Alaska due to immediate needs rather than future considerations. In order to solve the problem, they lost a valuable resource for Russia.Conclusively, the Alaska Purchase should not have been done as it has had a significant impact that will remain throughout history.
Article Summary: In 1867, russia sold alaska to the united states for only $7,200,000. However, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the u.s.

Article Title: Archaeologists found 500 Iron Age iron bars in Austria’s Danube, revealing a 1-tonne cargo transported 2,000 years ago
Article Text:
PC: Cambridge University Press

How the 500 iron bars were discovered at Deinham

PC: Cambridge University Press

What did radiocarbon dating reveal about the iron bars

How were the iron bars transported along the Danube

How large was the Iron Age iron cargo found at Deinham

Archaeologists have identified at least 500 forged iron bars recovered from the Danube in Upper Austria as the largest known assemblage of Iron Age iron in Europe. The discovery was made in 2019 during gravel extraction at Deinham, when workers found double-pointed iron objects in material taken from beneath the river’s water level. According to a research article published by Cambridge University Press titled ‘ A sunken ship cargo of 500 bipyramidal bars? Implications for La Tène period iron production and trade along the Danube ’, states that radiocarbon dating of three bars places the assemblage in the Late Iron Age, with dates falling between the fourth and first centuries BC.Workers at a gravel extraction site in Deinham identified at least 500 iron bars after discovering numerous double-pointed objects in 2019. The material had been removed from beneath the Danube’s water level, which disturbed and destroyed the original archaeological context. The finds were brought to the attention of the Federal Monuments Office, which was followed by the hand collection of additional pieces from the gravel heaps.A total of 540 fragments were recovered. From the material, researchers identified a minimum of 500 individual bars. Many of the bars are heavily corroded, while sand and gravel remain attached to their surfaces. In 2023, the recovered finds were donated to the Oberösterreichische Landes-Kultur GmbH in Linz, where they are now kept in permanent storage.The Deinham bars date to a later period than earlier examples of bipyramidal iron products. Researchers radiocarbon-dated samples from three bars, producing two probability peaks. One falls in the second half of the fourth century BC, while the other extends from the end of the third century into the second century BC. The later date range is consistent with archaeological evidence from comparable BLD6 bars.Based on their form and dating, the researchers classify the Deinham pieces as a new BLD6 variant of forged iron semi-products rather than cast ingots. Most complete bars are elongated and double-pointed, measuring an average of 285mm in length. They weigh an average of 2,070g, with individual complete bars ranging from 959g to 3,824g.The location of the finding provides clues about how the iron bars may have been transported. The bars were recovered from silted-up channels along the right bank of the Danube, near the entrance to the Eferding Basin. Similar iron-bar finds from Central European rivers are generally interpreted as cargo lost during transport or in shipwrecks.The researchers do not completely rule out deliberate deposition, but note that the uniform composition of the Deinham assemblage differs from more varied ritual deposits found in rivers. No remains of a boat were found with the bars, as the original archaeological context was disturbed during gravel extraction. The study considers river transport the most likely explanation and notes that Late Iron Age logboats could carry more than one tonne of cargo.The Deinham assemblage has an estimated total weight of 1,035kg, making it the largest known assemblage of Iron Age iron bars in Europe. The researchers say its combined weight provides evidence of the scale of iron production during the third and second centuries BC. They estimate that one tonne of iron could have produced about 500 swords, allowing for manufacturing losses, or around 8,000 nails. The researchers also indicate that the cargo may have originated further upstream, with the Manching, Kelheim and Upper Palatinate region considered the most plausible production area.
Article Summary: Workers at a gravel extraction site in deinham identified at least 500 iron bars after discovering numerous double-pointed objects in 2019. The bars date to a later period than earlier examples of bipyramidal iron products. They weigh an average of 2,070g, with individual complete bars ranging from 959g to 3,824g.
